Reviewed tracked-change and unexpected-untracked-path refusal, remote and revision pins, launcher/config/requirements/model hashes, Python dependency equality, loopback refusal, occupied-port behavior, runtime version, verified shutdown ancestry, MCP publication prohibition, documentation discoverability, and WP-015B-E boundaries. skipped_checks: The Playwright phone-browser matrix was not run because WP-015A changes only local generation tooling, compliance metadata, tests, and documentation; it changes no browser-facing gameplay, identity, reward UI, or approved runtime media.
Linux visual comparison and baseline generation were not run because the bounded smoke is external pipeline-health output, not a visual candidate or runtime asset.
Physical Android/iOS and Nimiq Pay testing was not run because no game or approved media behavior changed.
residual_risks: The archived SD 1.5 checkpoint is approved only for deterministic pipeline health smoke and non-product experiments. WP-015B must approve the actual model, workflow, prompts, inputs, output, and IP similarity before a master can become a product candidate.
MCP tools are discovered when Codex opens a client session. An already-open task may require a Codex restart after the loopback services start.

The installation is workstation-specific and externally maintained. Environment-variable path overrides and the clean-machine runbook reduce re-entry cost but do not replace a new review when any external revision, package, launcher, config, or model changes.
AutoSprite and the production animation/export path remain unverified and may block WP-015C; the workflow must stop rather than silently substitute another generator.
